route: scripted (procedural Blender geometry; no provider generation; face art reused from the P5-T6 UI atlas)

texturesSampled: ui/dice-d8 (shared UI atlas page, resident for the UI)
ui/dice-d8-glow (shared UI atlas glow page, the face emissive map)

lods: LOD0 only: a 40 mm die stays within the 1,500-triangle dice budget (DICE_LIMITS), so a LOD chain saves nothing measurable
bake: none: face art is the shared atlas page and brass is a factor (or the shared brass-polished set), so nothing is baked

frame.convention: src/dice/faces.ts die-local frame; identity orientation = DicePresenter's
frame.uv: TEXCOORD_0 is glTF (v down); loadDice flips v once so face UVs are in the UI atlas's bottom-left texture space

materialsUsed: factor-only polished brass named after the approved P4-T3 brass-polished set (bindable at runtime); the face slot samples the shared P5-T6 UI atlas page
license: Original work generated in Blender from a checked-in script; face art and style reference from Paul's paid Higgsfield plan (Terms of Use 4.4)

checks: face table (GLB extras and manifest) equals faces.ts and content/dice.ts
reimport gate (face-up UVs in the atlas cell, no mirrored UVs, Blender reimport)

approvals.notes: validate-generated-assets verdict is reported to the orchestrator, not self-recorded
original procedural geometry; face art from the P5-T6 atlas (its own provenance)
Paul approves the in-engine look (docs/blender-kit-project.md ruling 3)
blender-kit-pieces requires an independent >= 80/100 score; unscored means unaccepted

independentScore.scale: 0-100 visual fidelity to the art direction
independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the asset)

rubric.note: Up 8 from 18. The die is now a brass-bodied octahedron with dark panels, close to panel 4's d20 construction. The right die spans y 264 to 527 (263 px). A vertical scan at x=560 crosses the upper-left rail over y 311 to 331 (21 px) in two bevel facets (relL about 0.17 then 0.29), the equator band at x=600 spans y 375 to 394 (20 px, a lit facet at 0.17 over a shaded one at 0.07), and the lower-right rail at y=460 spans x 622 to 643. That is about 7.6% of die height, against the last score's 2 px rail and 5 px band, so the prior thickness fix is met. Points are lost because the rails are flat planar strips without panel 4's rounded, chunky bevel, and the shadow-side rail (relL 0.05 to 0.07 at y=460) is darker than the floor (0.094), so that edge of the silhouette loses its outline.

Up 6 from 13. The numerals are now amber, not cream. The top quartile of amber stroke pixels measures #C08C53 to #C08B4F on all four closeup numerals (H31 to 32, S 0.57 to 0.59), against the last score's #C2A580 at S 0.31 to 0.35, and the brass body is carried through every face. Through-body ghosting is gone from the lit faces. At the previous internal-edge coordinate (x 343 to 354, y 240) relL is now flat at 0.012 to 0.015 where it was 0.15 to 0.17. Points are lost on value and glow. The numerals sit at V 0.75 and relL 0.30, against candle amber #F3BE65 (relL about 0.57) and the reference d20's #FFC64B, so they read as copper paint more than lit amber. The glow drops from relL 0.066 one pixel outside the stroke to 0.023 at two pixels and to the far-glass level by about 10 px, while the reference numerals bleed visibly into their faces. The left die's grazing side face renders blue-grey with a pale #B28E76 numeral (S about 0.3), which is that face's own numeral seen at a grazing angle rather than a through-body ghost. The jewel corner flecks seen last time are gone (21 cool pixels on the right die), which the bible does not require for dice.

Up 2 from 11. The body now reads as dark smoked glass or enamel with faint ember specks: glass p20 to p70 inside the faces measures relL 0.005 to 0.020, down from 0.12 to 0.16, which fits the bible's enamel-face option. It shows no visible depth or refraction, so it reads closer to obsidian enamel than glass. The rails are uniform flat brass with no wear. Hue-masked rail relL runs p10 0.068, p50 0.159 and p90 0.197 on the right die, and the only bright highlight is the pale bevel edge (top 5% #AF9457 to #D4B578). At grazing angles the glass turns a neutral blue-grey (#54534E to #5D5048, S under 0.15, relL 0.09) on the left die's side face, which brings back the old frosted-plastic look on that face. That grey covers 0 to 3.6% of die pixels across the eight lineup dice.

Up 4 from 7. The face glass is now near warm black (#1F0E06 to #2F231D, relL 0.005 to 0.020, against #231D1A), and the die separates from the walnut floor (#724F37, relL 0.094) at about 3:1 on the glass, up from 1.2 to 1.5:1. The numeral saturation now matches candle amber (S 0.57 to 0.59 against 0.58), though the hue sits more orange (H31 to 32 against H37) and the value is low (V 0.75 against 0.95). The rails are mustard-olive (median #876B30, H41, S 0.64, V 0.53) against polished brass #DEC16A (V 0.87), the same shortfall as the d6. The blue-grey grazing face is off-palette.

Up 5 from 4. Numeral-core-to-glass contrast measures 5.54:1 (left die "1"), 6.43:1 (left "3"), 5.15:1 (right "7") and 6.27:1 (right "3"), median about 5.9:1, against about 2.5:1 last time. All eight lineup dice measure 5.43 to 6.22:1, and every one clears 4.5:1. With the ghosts gone, the face-up numeral is the clearest mark on each die. Numeral strokes are 8 to 15 px in the closeup and readable on the 64 to 93 px lineup dice. A point is held back for the low numeral value and the grey grazing face, which show a second, washed-out numeral on some dice. The evidence is desktop only.

topFixes: Brighten the numerals toward lit candle amber. The core is #C08C53 (relL 0.30, V 0.75, H31), against #F3BE65 (relL about 0.57) and the reference #FFC64B. Raise the emissive value and shift the hue slightly toward yellow (H35 to 37) while keeping S at least 0.55, and widen the glow so it bleeds 3 to 6 px into the face instead of falling to near black within 2 px.

Fix the grazing-angle grey on the glass. The left die's side face renders blue-grey #54534E (S under 0.15) with a washed-out numeral, and the same grey covers up to 3.6% of die pixels in the lineup. Lower the Fresnel or specular reflection on the glass panels, or tint the environment reflection warm, so oblique faces stay dark smoked glass.

Polish the brass rails. The median is #876B30 (V 0.53) against #DEC16A (V 0.87), and the shadow-side rail (relL 0.05 to 0.07) falls below the floor (0.094) so that edge disappears. Lift the base colour and roughness response, add a rounded bevel highlight and edge wear, and keep a rim value above the floor on the shadow side.
Round the rails into chunkier bevels like panel 4's d20. The current rails are flat two-facet strips about 20 px on a 263 px die. A rounded profile would give them a continuous specular roll.
independentScore.method: Independent reviewer (did not build the asset). I read the dice and palette sections of docs/art-bible.md and the previous independentScore in assets-source/dice/glass-d8/provenance.json, and I did not open any author status or self-score file in /tmp. Primary evidence was the in-engine stills of commit 68eca00 through the runtime loader (Apple M4, ANGLE Metal): docs/verification/p5-dice-glass-d8.jpg and p5-dice-glass-d8-lineup.jpg, both 960x640, cropped and upscaled 2x to 4x for inspection. The Blender review sheet assets-source/dice/dice.review-sheet.jpg was viewed for context only. The reference was L-board-1.png panel 4, cropped at (60,956)-(750,1490). Measurements used Pillow and NumPy under python3 -I: median sRGB in fixed crop boxes, hue-masked brass (H38 to 60, S above 0.3, cross-checked at S above 0.45), pixel scans across frames, rails and walls, and ring or distance profiles around pips and numerals. Numeral cores are the top quartile of amber stroke pixels (H15 to 38, S above 0.45, relL above 0.15). An earlier top-5% non-brass sample was discarded because rail highlights (H41 to 44) leaked into it. Glass is the relL below 0.06 population in each face box. Contrast ratios are WCAG (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on relative luminance. The deltas against the previous score are approximate, because these stills now bind the glow pages as the runtime does and the earlier stills showed less emission. All evidence is desktop only, with no headset capture. Date 2026-11-16.
